headline: Rate recovery and nuclear relief lift Xcel's earnings
summary_short: Xcel Energy's Q2 2026 diluted EPS rose 24% y/y to $0.93 on higher recovery of electric and gas infrastructure investment, even as revenue fell 5.1% y/y to $3.12B on Minnesota rate-case refunds and seasonal effects.
summary_long: Second-quarter diluted EPS rose 24% y/y to $0.93 (basic $0.94), driven mainly by higher recovery of electric and gas infrastructure investment across all four operating utilities, partly offset by higher interest and financing costs. Revenue fell 5.1% y/y to $3.12B, primarily reflecting interim rate refunds in the Minnesota Electric Rate Case — a reduction the company says was more than offset by a corresponding cut to depreciation expense from approved nuclear-plant life extensions. Earnings from equity-method investments rose $84M on unrealized gains in energy-technology funds. Cash grew to $2.01B and long-term debt rose to $36.9B, funding continued capex in renewable generation and transmission. Full-year 2026 ongoing EPS guidance stands at $4.04-$4.16 per share.

drivers.explanation: Q2 electric revenue fell mainly on recognition of interim rate refunds in the Minnesota Electric Rate Case; the reduction was more than offset by a corresponding cut to depreciation from nuclear-plant life extensions.
Higher recovery of electric and natural gas infrastructure investment across all four operating companies, partly offset by higher interest and financing costs from increased debt levels.
Depreciation and amortization fell $60M in Q2 on recognition of nuclear life-extension depreciation reductions, while O&M rose modestly on higher generation costs.
Earnings from equity-method investments rose $84M on unrealized gains in energy-technology fund interests, adding to growth alongside base rate recovery.
New first-mortgage-bond and junior subordinated note issuances across Xcel's utility subsidiaries funded continued capex in renewable generation and transmission system investment.
2026 ongoing EPS guidance stands at $4.04-$4.16 per share; the filing doesn't state whether this range is changed from prior guidance.
